chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ays ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about the performer of Tamattu' who enters on the Day of Tarwiyah and has no sacrificial animal with him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'So he should not fast that day, nor the Day of Arafah, and he should take a pre-dawn meal on the night of al-Hasbah, so he would be fasting in the morning, and it would be the Day of Nafar, and he would fast the two days after it.'

key_terms.لَيْلَةَ الْحَصْبَةِ: The night of al-Hasah, a specific night in the Hajj rituals
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعٍ: A pilgrim who performs Umrah and Hajj separately, combining them with a single Ihram
key_terms.هَدْيٌ: Sacrificial animal offered by the pilgrim
key_terms.يَوْمَ التَّرْوِيَةِ: The 8th of Dhu al-Hijjah, known as the Day of Tarwiyah
key_terms.يَوْمَ عَرَفَةَ: The 9th of Dhu al-Hijjah, the Day of Arafah
key_terms.يَوْمُ النَّفْرِ: The Day of Nafar, referring to the departure from Mina

ai.seo_question: What are the fasting obligations for a Mutamatti' pilgrerim who lacks a sacrificial animal?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the specific fasting expiation for a Mutamatti' pilgrim lacking the means for a sacrificial animal, prescribing fasts on the Day of Tarwiyah, the Day of Arafah, and the two days following the Day of Nafar. It highlights the Shia juristic view that these days serve as a substitute for the hady, ensuring the pilgrim's Hajj remains valid despite financial constraints. The ruling underscores the flexibility in Shia fiqh to accommodate varying economic conditions while maintaining ritual integrity.
